name: The Hawthorne effect
purpose: Why did productivity rise whatever the researchers changed?

parts.label: Care
points: Showing people their work matters raises performance

parts.label: Informal organisation
points: Group morale and informal leaders matter more than formal rules

parts.label: Group norms
points: Don't produce too much or too little

apply: Use it to explain why perks or attention alone change behaviour – and how peer norms can cap output
pitfalls: It is the start of the human relations school, not of scientific management

name: Contribution–retribution equilibrium (psychological contract)
purpose: Why do people join, stay and contribute – and what happens when the balance breaks?
apply: List retributions and contributions with case facts
Judge the balance as the employees perceive it
Predict reactions: reduce contribution, raise retribution, exit (Hirschman)
pitfalls: Only perceptions count, not objective values
example: Google: great pay and perks, but heavy workload, little recognition and conformism.

name: Exit, voice and loyalty
purpose: How do people react when an organisation no longer meets their expectations?

parts.label: Loyalty
points: Stay and accept – attachment or resignation

parts.label: Exit
points: Leave silently – needs an external labour market

parts.label: Voice
points: Stay and protest, hoping for change

apply: Classify each actor's reaction in the case and explain it by alternatives and attachment

name: Three incentive and control mechanisms
purpose: How does an organisation get people to contribute?
apply: Describe the mix in the case and whether it fits the people and the work
pitfalls: All three are used in variable proportions
